sections.h2: What is the fastest way to sell a Passaic house?
sections.html:
Selling for cash as the house stands is usually the shortest path, since it drops repairs, showings and a buyer's loan approval. A listing or private sale takes longer. Every route, though, has to clear the city's occupancy certificate and fire certification before closing.

Many Passaic buildings hold more than one unit, and owners live in just 23.8 percent of homes. Sellers here are often landlords, heirs, or owners of condos and co-ops. Whichever you are, gather these items first:

  • The deed and the block and lot numbers, which every city application asks for.
  • Tenant leases and rent rolls, if any unit is occupied.
  • Mortgage payoff figures and any open municipal charges.
  • The name the buyer will take title in, because Passaic issues the occupancy certificate under the buyer's name.

Passaic is a dense city of 71,337 residents in the 2025 estimate, packed into 3.13 square miles. Renters outnumber owners about three to one, and households run large at an average of 3.29 people across 21,151 households. The median owned home is valued at $429,900, typical rent is $1,465 and median household income is $55,371.

Condo and co-op owners in Passaic Park, in complexes such as the 21-floor Carlton Tower and the Barry Gardens garden apartments, should ask their association what documents a buyer needs. About 72.3 percent of residents speak another language at home, so bilingual listing and closing papers can help buyers follow what they sign.

A sale in Passaic needs two approvals: an occupancy certificate, and a smoke detector and carbon monoxide certification. The one-family application goes to the Division of Housing under Inspections and Code. It asks for the seller's details and the buyer's name, because the certificate is issued to the buyer. A company buying through an LLC or corporation must supply the registered agent and the certificate of formation.

Inspection and violation reports are emailed to both seller and buyer, and extra copies require an OPRA request. The fire certification stays valid for three months and covers only the buyer named on it, so schedule the inspection close to the closing date.

The fire inspector looks for a smoke detector on each level, detectors and a carbon monoxide alarm outside every sleeping area, working units, and a fire extinguisher within ten feet of the kitchen. A 90-day temporary certification is available when items fail. The occupancy certificate confirms the property meets Passaic's zoning and property maintenance laws. It does not replace construction permits or health approvals. Condo, one, two and three family homes all use the fire form.

sections.h2: How the Passaic approval process runs
sections.html:
Start the paperwork once you have a signed contract and the buyer's exact legal name. File the occupancy application with the Division of Housing, then book the fire inspection with Fire Prevention. If you want the faster handling, ask for the $300 expedite option when you file.

When the inspector finds problems, you have two ways forward. Fix the items and request a reinspection at $25, or ask for the 90-day temporary fire certification and agree with the buyer on who finishes the work. Tell your closing attorney which route you chose so the closing date reflects it.

Bring the same set of papers to every office: the deed, block and lot numbers, payoff figures and, for an entity buyer, the registered agent and certificate of formation. A short call to the Division of Housing before you file saves a second trip.

Trenton charges a Realty Transfer Fee, and in Passaic the seller pays it when the deed is recorded. Above $350,000 the schedule opens at $2.90 per $500 of price. At or below that line it runs $2.00, $3.35 or $3.90 per $500, depending on the band. A parent leaving a house to a child, or an heir taking title from a parent, can usually claim an exemption on a notarized Form RTF-1 filed with the deed.

A GIT/REP form is recorded alongside the deed too. Its job is to tell the State whether an out-of-state seller owes prepaid income tax, and the person who signs the deed fills it out. Your attorney or closing agent normally prepares the deed, the fee paperwork and this form, and you sign at the closing table.

Flood disclosure has been mandatory since March 20, 2024. The river borders the city, so check the FEMA zone for your lot in the DEP Flood Risk Notification Tool and answer the statement honestly before the buyer is bound.

sections.h2: How to appeal your Passaic assessment
sections.html:
An owner who thinks the city's figure is too high files Form A-1 with the Passaic County Board of Taxation. The board must have it by April 1, or by May 1 where Passaic has carried out a revaluation or reassessment.

You carry the proof. Show that the assessment is out of line with market value or with the district's common level range. Anything assessed above $1,000,000 can go straight to the State Tax Court, and a county board decision can be carried to that court within 45 days. The city tax collector can give you your balance and open charges. The county board can tell you where to deliver the petition and how its hearings are scheduled.

Before you file, pull your latest assessment notice and compare it with what similar homes nearby have sold for. Have your block and lot numbers ready, since the petition and every city form key off them. If you are selling this year, tell your attorney about the appeal so any refund or balance is handled at closing.

sections.h2: What a cash sale skips in Passaic
sections.html:
A cash buyer taking the house as it stands removes the repair list, the showings and the wait for a lender. It does not remove the city's certificates. The occupancy certificate and fire certification are still needed, and the buyer's name still goes on both.

Before you accept an offer, ask who files the occupancy application, who pays the $65 certificate fee and any $300 expedite charge, and who pays for a fire reinspection. For a multi-unit building, add the lease and rent roll question: tell the buyer which units are occupied and on what terms. Compare offers by what you net after payoff, transfer fee and carrying costs.

Passaic's mix of two and three family buildings, condos and co-ops means the buyer's plan matters. An investor keeping tenants cares about the leases, while an owner-occupant needs a vacant unit at closing. Settle that in writing before the certificate application goes in, because the form asks who will take title and the city will not issue the certificate until it has that name.

faqs.q: Whose name goes on the Passaic occupancy certificate?
faqs.a: The buyer's. The one-family application issues the certificate under the buyer's name, and an LLC buyer must supply its registered agent and certificate of formation.

faqs.q: What does the Passaic occupancy certificate cost?
faqs.a: The fee is $65 on the one-family application, plus a $300 expedite charge if you need faster handling.

faqs.q: How long does the fire certification last?
faqs.a: Three months from approval, and only for the person named on it. When the inspection finds problems, a 90-day temporary certification can be issued.

faqs.q: Does the seller cover the state transfer fee in Passaic?
faqs.a: Yes. The State bills the seller at recording, and the fee steps up with the sale price.

faqs.q: Where does a Passaic owner take an assessment appeal?
faqs.a: To the Passaic County Board of Taxation, by April 1, or May 1 after a revaluation. Owners above $1,000,000 in assessed value may skip ahead to Tax Court.
